title: Act II, Scene II
focus: the murder and its first guilt

teacherSummary.text: Lady Macbeth waits, saying she would have killed Duncan herself had he not resembled her father as he slept. Macbeth returns from the murder with bloody hands, haunted that he could not say 'Amen' and that a voice cried 'Macbeth does murder sleep.' He has carried the daggers away; he refuses to return, so she takes them back and smears the grooms with blood. Knocking sounds at the gate; Macbeth says all great Neptune's ocean could not wash the blood from his hand, and wishes the knocking could wake Duncan.

context.history: The murder happens offstage; Shakespeare shows its aftermath rather than the act. Blood, sleep and hands become the play's key image clusters.

significance: The scene reverses positions: Macbeth falls apart and Lady Macbeth stays controlled ('A little water clears us of this deed'). Her line sets up the sleepwalking scene, where water no longer clears anything.

hsFreshman.note: Use the scaffolds for literal and inferential items; require one quotation for every inferential answer.
